{{short description|In mathematics, representation of a reductive algebraic group}}
In [[representation theory]], a branch of mathematics, the '''Whittaker model''' is a realization of a [[Group representation|representation]] of a [[reductive algebraic group]] such as ''GL''<sub>2</sub> over a [[finite field|finite]] or [[local field|local]] or [[global field]] on a space of functions on the group. It is named after [[E. T. Whittaker]] even though he never worked in this area, because {{harvs|last=Jacquet|year1=1966|year2=1967}} pointed out that for the group SL<sub>2</sub>('''R''')  some of the functions involved in the representation are [[Whittaker function]]s.

[[Irreducible representation]]s without a Whittaker model are sometimes called "degenerate", and those with a Whittaker model are sometimes called "generic". The representation [[θ10|''θ''<sub>10</sub>]] of the [[symplectic group]] Sp<sub>4</sub> is the simplest example of a degenerate representation.

==Whittaker models for GL<sub>2</sub>==

If ''G'' is the [[algebraic group]] ''GL''<sub>2</sub> and '''F''' is a local field, and {{math|''τ''}} is a fixed non-trivial [[Character theory|character]] of the additive group of '''F''' and {{pi}} is an irreducible representation of a general linear group ''G''('''F'''), then the Whittaker model for {{pi}} is a representation {{pi}} on a space of  functions ''ƒ'' on ''G''('''F''') satisfying

:<math>f\left(\begin{pmatrix}1 & b \\ 0 & 1\end{pmatrix}g\right) = \tau(b)f(g). </math>

{{harvtxt|Jacquet|Langlands|1970}} used Whittaker models to assign L-functions to [[admissible representation]]s of ''GL''<sub>2</sub>.

==Whittaker models for GL<sub>''n''</sub>==

Let <math>G</math> be the [[general linear group]] <math>\operatorname{GL}_n</math>, <math>\psi</math> a smooth complex valued non-trivial additive character of <math>F</math> and <math>U</math> the subgroup of <math>\operatorname{GL}_n</math> consisting of unipotent upper triangular matrices. A non-degenerate character on <math>U</math> is of the form

:<math>\chi(u)=\psi(\alpha_1 x_{12}+\alpha_2 x_{23}+\cdots+\alpha_{n-1}x_{n-1n}),</math>

for <math>u=(x_{ij})</math> ∈ <math>U</math> and non-zero <math>\alpha_1, \ldots, \alpha_{n-1}</math> ∈ <math>F</math>. If <math>(\pi,V)</math> is a smooth representation of <math>G(F)</math>, a '''Whittaker functional''' <math>\lambda</math> is a continuous linear functional on <math>V</math> such that <math>\lambda(\pi(u)v)=\chi(u)\lambda(v)</math> for all <math>u</math> ∈ <math>U</math>, <math>v</math> ∈ <math>V</math>. '''Multiplicity one''' states that, for <math>\pi</math> unitary irreducible, the space of Whittaker functionals has dimension at most equal to one.

==Whittaker models for reductive groups==

If ''G'' is a split reductive group and ''U'' is the unipotent radical of  a Borel subgroup ''B'', then a Whittaker model for a representation is an embedding of it into the induced ([[Gelfand–Graev representation|Gelfand–Graev]]) representation Ind{{su|b=''U''|p=''G''}}({{math|''χ''}}), where {{math|''χ''}} is a non-degenerate character of ''U'', such as the sum of the characters corresponding to simple roots.
